4.89.m: Therefore, O brāhmaṇa, what is surprising here? Does not Death surely destroy a mere skeleton?

4.89.m: Verily, what is not destined to be can never come to be anywhere;

4.89.m: and what is destined to be cannot fail to be. Therefore, the wise are not bewildered.”
Hearing what was spoken by Śambhu, that foremost of munis
said: “It is indeed true, what the Lord has said.
Whatever was bound to happen has happened; there is no doubt in this.
Yet one thought greatly torments and agitates my mind:
In truth, nothing diminishes for you, nor does anything increase.
Because you are immutable and full, whence could there be loss or gain in you?
Alas, where will this wretched world go, left without a Lord?
For starting from this day, no one will worship you,
since the progenitor Dakṣa did not invite you to the sacrifice.
Seeing that disrespect today, even gods, seers, and mortals
will show disrespect to you. What is sovereignty to those who are disrespected?
Those who have suffered contempt in the world, even if they have conquered the fear of death,
though endowed with sovereignty—how can they be a vessel of honor?
What is the use of long life or abundant wealth to those
whose wealth is honor, yet who meet with disrespect at every step in this world?
Senseless and subject to contempt, though living, they are not fit for fame.
Blessed are those whose wealth is honor; far better is that truly virtuous woman Satī,
who, on hearing revilement of you, counted her own life as a blade of grass.”
Hearing this and fully knowing the demise of Satī, Mahākāla [said]:

4.89.m: Bowing to the Lord and wielding a massive bhuśuṇḍī, he spoke:

4.89.m: “Give me your command, O Father! What supreme service shall I do for you?

4.89.m: then at your command, I will render his weapons blunt.

4.89.m: Who are the Danujas and sons of Diti? Wretched, weak from petty causes!

4.89.m: And if anyone among them displays arrogance, I shall strike him down.

4.89.m: I will bind Time in battle, or inflict death upon Death himself.
When I am enraged upon the battlefield, among the stationary and moving beings here,
by your power, O Great Lord, no one shall remain standing.
By the stamp of the sole of my foot, this circle of the earth,

4.89.m: What need of many words? Give your command; nothing is impossible for me.
Having obtained the power of your feet, know whatever was unthought of to be accomplished today.”
Hearing this vow of his, the Lord considered the deed already accomplished.
Joyfully, as if he had fully achieved his goal, he replied to him:
“You are indeed a great hero, O auspicious one, among all my gaṇas here.

4.89.m: Execute my task swiftly: bring the sacrifice of Dakṣa to destruction!”

4.89.m: Placing that supreme command upon his head,
he circumambulated Hara and departed with immense speed.

other fierce gaṇas, numbering a hundred crores.

4.89.m: As Vīrabhadra went, some of those gaṇas went ahead;
some followed behind him, and some went at his sides.
The sky was overcome by them, their splendor fanning the sun;

uprooting great trees, some reached the sacrificial enclosure.

some gaṇas, raging with fury, demolished the pavilion;
some, trident in hand, dug up the altars;
others ate the oblations, and others drank the clotted butter;
some destroyed heaps of food resembling mountains;
some fed on milk rice, and some drank milk;

4.89.m: some seized the mountain made of jewels previously constructed.

4.89.m: By one, the god Bhaga was made eyeless as he watched;

4.89.m: One, seeing Sarasvatī fleeing, made her noseless;
the two lips of Aditi were cut off by another in anger.

someone forcibly tore out the tongue of Agni.

4.89.m: someone bound Yama in nooses and asked: "What sort of righteousness is this,

4.89.m: in which righteousness Maheśa is not worshipped first?"
Another seized Nairṛta by the hair, shook him repeatedly,
and struck him with his foot, saying: "An oblation destitute of Īśvara was eaten by you!"
Another seized Kubera by his feet, shook him violently,
and made him vomit repeatedly the sacrificial oblations he had consumed.

4.89.m: Seeing the sacrificial arena resembling a cremation ground, having been reduced

4.89.m: "O gaṇas, behold the state of the undertakings commenced by the wicked
who are without Īśvara! Whence this malice toward Maheśvara?

4.89.m: Where is that evil-mannered Dakṣa? And where are the gods who partake of the sacrifice?
Seize them all and bring them here! Go swiftly, O gaṇas!"

4.89.m: Having received that command of Vīrabhadra, those pramathas quickly—
as soon as they rushed forward, an enraged wielder of the mace [Viṣṇu] was seen.
By him, all those pramathas of great strength and valor
were reduced to the condition of dry leaves and grass, as if by a whirlwind.
Then, when all the Pramathas had fled out of fear of Hari,
that Vīrabhadra grew enraged, resembling the fire of cosmic dissolution. (61)
And he saw before him the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, praised by his own attendants,
countless, four-armed ones of great strength who had conquered Daityas, (62)
attended by bearers of discs, clubs, swords, and bows.
Then Vīrabhadra, seeing that slayer of the Daityas, said: (63)
“You, however, are the Puruṣa of the sacrifice here, the initiator of the great sacrifice,
the protector, by your own valor, of Dakṣa, the enemy of the three-eyed Lord. (64)

4.89.s: kiṃ vā dakṣaṃ samānīya dehi yudhyasva vā mayā ..
4.89.d: किं वा दक्षं समानीय देहि युध्यस्व वा मया ..
4.89.m: Either bring Dakṣa here and hand him over, or fight with me!

4.89.d: न दास्यसि च चेद्दक्षं ततस्तं रक्ष यत्नतः .. 65 ..
4.89.m: And if you will not surrender Dakṣa, then protect him with all effort! (65)

4.89.m: Being pleased, Śambhu gave you the Sudarśana discus,

Viṣṇu, wishing to test his strength, spoke to Vīrabhadra: (68)

4.89.m: “Ah, you are almost a son to Śambhu, the foremost among the Gaṇas!

श्रुत्वा गंगेश माहात्म्यं न नरो निरयी भवेत् ..
लभेच्च पुण्यसंभारं चिंतितं चाधिगच्छति .. 11 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीति साहस्र्यां संहितायां चतुथें काशीखंड उत्तरार्धे गंगेश्वरमहिमाख्यानं नामैकनवतितमोऽध्यायः .. 91 ..
4.91.m: Skanda said: / “The glory of Pārvatīśa has been told to you by me, O sinless one. / Now hear, O sage, the origin of Gaṅgeśvara, / hearing which one obtains the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā anywhere. / When the Gaṅgā came to the holy pool Cakrapuṣkariṇī / together with that descendant of Dilīpa in this Ānandakānana, / realizing the peerless power of the sacred field due to Śambhu’s possession of it, / and remembering the transcendent fruit of establishing a liṅga in Kāśī, / an auspicious liṅga was established by Gaṅgā to the east of Viśveśa. / Sight of the liṅga Gaṅgeśvara is very hard to obtain in Kāśī; / and whoever worships Gaṅgeśa on the Daśaharā day, / the sin of a thousand births is wiped away in an instant. / In the Kali age the Gaṅgeśvara liṅga will become mostly hidden; / darśana of it produces merit for people. / By whom the Gaṅgeśvara liṅga, exceedingly rare in Kāśī, is seen, / the Gaṅgā in embodied form is seen by him, no doubt. / The Gaṅgā that takes away all impurities will be very hard to reach in the Kali age, / there is no doubt, O son of Mitrāvaruṇa; / even more so, when the Kali age has arrived, Kāśī is exceedingly hard to reach; / even rarer than that in Kāśī is the liṅga named Gaṅgeśvara, / the sight of which brings about the destruction of men’s sins. / Hearing the māhātmya of Gaṅgeśa, a person will not fall into hell; / he obtains an abundance of merit and attains whatever he desires.” / Thus ends the ninety-first chapter, titled “Account of the Glory of Gaṅgeśvara”, in the latter half of the Kāśīkhaṇḍa in the eighty-one-thousand-verse collection of the glorious Skandapurāṇa.

4.92.m: Skanda said:
“I shall tell you, O sage, the māhātmya of Narmadeśa,
by the mere recollection of which there is destruction of great sins.
At the beginning of this Vārāhakalpa, the foremost sages asked:

4.92.s: āpṛcchi kā saricchreṣṭhā vada tāṃ tvaṃ mṛkaṃḍaja ..2..
4.92.d: आपृच्छि का सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा वद तां त्वं मृकंडज ..2..
4.92.m: ‘Which river is the best? Tell us that, O son of Mṛkaṇḍu.’
Mārkaṇḍeya said:

4.92.s: śṛṇudhvaṃ munayaḥ sarve saṃti nadyaḥ paraḥśatam ..
4.92.d: शृणुध्वं मुनयः सर्वे संति नद्यः परःशतम् ..
4.92.m: ‘Listen, all you sages: there are more than a hundred rivers.
All are destroyers of sin, all grant virtue.
Superior to all rivers are those that reach the ocean;
even among them, most exalted are the best of rivers:

4.92.s: gaṃgā ca yamunācātha narmadā ca sarasvatī ..
4.92.d: गंगा च यमुनाचाथ नर्मदा च सरस्वती ..
4.92.m: the Gaṅgā, the Yamunā, the Narmadā, and the Sarasvatī.
This sacred quartet stands foremost among rivers, O best of sages.
Gaṅgā is the embodiment of the Ṛgveda, and Yamunā surely of the Yajurveda;
Narmadā is the embodiment of the Sāmaveda, and Sarasvatī of the Atharvaveda.
Gaṅgā is the origin of all rivers and the filler of the ocean;
no river here can attain equality with Gaṅgā.
However, formerly Revā performed severe austerity for a very long time,
and the Creator, ready to grant boons, was prayed to thus, O best of beings:

4.92.s: gaṃgā sāmyaṃ vidhe dehi prasannosi yadi prabho ..
4.92.d: गंगा साम्यं विधे देहि प्रसन्नोसि यदि प्रभो ..
4.92.m: “Grant me equality with Gaṅgā, O Creator, if you are pleased, O Lord!”
Then Brahmā said to Narmadā with a smile:
“If equality with the Three-Eyed Lord can be attained by anyone else,
then equality with Gaṅgā can be attained by another river.
If another male anywhere could be equal to Puruṣottama,

4.92.s: srotasvinī tadā sāmyaṃ labhate gaṃgayā parā .. 11 ..
4.92.d: स्रोतस्विनी तदा साम्यं लभते गंगया परा .. 11 ..
4.92.m: only then could another stream attain equality with Gaṅgā.”

4.92.s: yadi gaurī samā nārī kvacidanyā bhavediha ..
4.92.d: यदि गौरी समा नारी क्वचिदन्या भवेदिह ..
4.92.m: If any other woman in this world could be equal to Gaurī,
only then would another river here attain equality with the heavenly river.
If any city could be equal to this city of Kāśī,
then another river might attain equality with the river of heaven.
Hearing these words of Brahmā, the Narmadā, best of rivers,
renounced the boon from the Creator and went to the city of Vārāṇasī.
Indeed, of all meritorious acts, compared to the consecration of a liṅga in Kāśī,
no other deed bringing greater welfare has been taught by anyone.

4.92.s: atha sā narmadā puṇyā vidhipūrvāṃ pratiṣṭhitim ..
4.92.d: अथ सा नर्मदा पुण्या विधिपूर्वां प्रतिष्ठितिम् ..
4.92.m: Then that holy Narmadā performed the consecration according to the prescribed rites
at the Pilipilātīrtha, near the Triviṣṭapa [liṅga].
Then Śambhu became pleased with that auspicious-natured river:
"Choose a boon, O fortunate one, whatever pleases you, O sinless lady."
Hearing this, the Revā, best of rivers, said to Maheśvara:

4.92.s: kiṃ vareṇeha deveśa bhṛśaṃ tucchena dhūrjaṭe .. .. 18 ..
4.92.d: किं वरेणेह देवेश भृशं तुच्छेन धूर्जटे .. .. 18 ..
4.92.m: "What need is there for a boon here, O Lord of gods, Dhūrjaṭi, which is utterly trivial?
May I have unswerving devotion to your two feet, O Maheśvara."
Hearing this, [the Lord] was exceedingly delighted by the peerless speech of the Revā,

4.92.s: provāca ca sariccheṣṭhe tvayoktaṃ yattathāstu tat ..
4.92.d: प्रोवाच च सरिच्छेष्ठे त्वयोक्तं यत्तथास्तु तत् ..
4.92.m: and said: "O best of rivers, let it be as you have spoken.
Accept [it], O abode of merit! I bestow another boon:

4.92.s: yāvaṃtyo dṛṣadaḥ saṃti tava rodhasi narmade ..
4.92.d: यावंत्यो दृषदः संति तव रोधसि नर्मदे ..
4.92.m: As many stones as there are on your bank, O Narmadā,
so many shall have the form of liṅgas, by my boon.

4.92.s: anyaṃ ca te varaṃ dadyā tamapyākarṇayottamam ..
4.92.d: अन्यं च ते वरं दद्या तमप्याकर्णयोत्तमम् ..
4.92.m: And I grant you another excellent boon; listen to that as well,
which in truth is difficult to attain even through heaps of sacrifices and austerities:
The Gaṅgā removes sins immediately; the Yamunā in seven days;
the Sarasvatī in three days; but you, O Revā, through mere sight.

4.92.s: aparaṃ ca varaṃ dadyāṃ narmade darśanāghahe ..
4.92.d: अपरं च वरं दद्यां नर्मदे दर्शनाघहे ..
4.92.m: And I grant another boon, O Narmadā, destroyer of sins by mere sight:
the liṅga established by you, named Narmadeśvara,
that most sacred liṅga shall bestow eternal liberation.
Seeing those who are devoted to this liṅga, the son of Sūrya (Yama)
will bow with effort, for the increase of his great welfare.
There are many liṅgas in Kāśī at every step, O goddess,

4.92.s: paraṃ hi narmadeśasya mahimā kopi cādbhutaḥ ..
4.92.d: परं हि नर्मदेशस्य महिमा कोपि चाद्भुतः ..
4.92.m: yet the greatness of Narmadeśa is indescribable and wonderful."
Having spoken thus, the Lord of the lords of gods merged into that liṅga.
The Narmadā also rejoiced, having attained wondrous purity,
and returned to her own region, removing sins upon mere sight.
Having heard those words of the sage born of Mṛkaṇḍu, those best of sages

4.92.s: prahṛṣṭacetaso jātāścakruḥ svaṃ svaṃ tato hitam .. 29 ..
4.92.d: प्रहृष्टचेतसो जाताश्चक्रुः स्वं स्वं ततो हितम् .. 29 ..
4.92.m: became delighted in mind and then attended to their respective welfare.
Skanda said:
Having heard the greatness of Narmadeśa, a person endowed with devotion,
shedding the slough of sin, will attain supreme knowledge.

4.92.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ caturthe kāśīkhaṃḍa uttarārdhe narmadeśvarākhyānaṃ nāma dvinavatitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 92 ..
4.92.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां चतुर्थे काशीखंड उत्तरार्धे नर्मदेश्वराख्यानं नाम द्विनवतितमोऽध्यायः .. 92 ..
4.92.m: Thus ends the ninety-second chapter, named 'The Narrative of Narmadeśvara', in the second half of the Kāśīkhaṇḍa, in the fourth [part of] the venerable Skandapurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

4.93.m: Agastya said:
"The greatness of Narmadeśa, which destroys sins, has been heard.
Now tell [me], O Skanda, of the origin of Satīśvara."
Skanda said:

4.93.s: mitrāvaruṇasaṃbhūta kathayāmi kathāṃ śṛṇu .. yathā satīśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ kāśyāmāvirbabhūva ha .. 2 ..
4.93.d: मित्रावरुणसंभूत कथयामि कथां शृणु .. यथा सतीश्वरं लिंगं काश्यामाविर्बभूव ह .. 2 ..
4.93.m: "O one born of Mitra and Varuṇa, I shall tell the story; listen to how the liṅga Satīśvara appeared in Kāśī.
Formerly, O sage, Brahmā performed very great austerity.
Pleased by that austerity, the Lord of gods became the grantor of boons,
and he, exceedingly fond of brahmins,
the omniscient lord, the Self of all worlds, said to Brahmā: 'Choose a boon, O creator of worlds!'"
Brahmā said:

4.93.s: yadi prasanno deveśa varaṃ dāsyasi vāṃchitam ..
4.93.d: यदि प्रसन्नो देवेश वरं दास्यसि वांछितम् ..
4.93.m: "If, being pleased, O Lord of gods, you will grant the desired boon,

4.93.s: tadā tvaṃ me bhava suto devī dakṣasutā'stu ca .. 5 ..
4.93.d: तदा त्वं मे भव सुतो देवी दक्षसुताऽस्तु च .. 5 ..
4.93.m: then become my son, and let the Goddess become the daughter of Dakṣa."

4.93.s: iti śrutvā mahādevaḥ sarvado brahmaṇo varam ..
4.93.d: इति श्रुत्वा महादेवः सर्वदो ब्रह्मणो वरम् ..
4.93.m: Hearing this boon sought by Brahmā, Mahādeva, the granter of all,
smiled, looked at the Goddess's face, and said to the four-faced [creator]:
"O Brahmā, let your desire be fulfilled; what is not to be given [to you], O grandfather?"
Having said this, the moon-bearing Lord manifested from Brahmā's forehead.
Weeping, lying on his back, he looked at the face of Brahmā.

4.93.s: tato brahmāpi taṃ bālaṃ rudaṃtaṃ pravilokya ca .. 8 ..
4.93.d: ततो ब्रह्मापि तं बालं रुदंतं प्रविलोक्य च .. 8 ..
4.93.m: Then Brahmā also, seeing that weeping child,

4.93.s: kiṃ māṃ janakamāpyāpi tvaṃ rodiṣi muhurmuhuḥ ..
4.93.d: किं मां जनकमाप्यापि त्वं रोदिषि मुहुर्मुहुः ..
4.93.m: [said]: 'Why, even after having attained me as your father, do you weep again and again?'
Hearing this, the infant replied to what was spoken by Parameṣṭhin.

4.93.s: nāmne rodimi me sraṣṭurnāma dehi pitāmaha ..
4.93.d: नाम्ने रोदिमि मे स्रष्टुर्नाम देहि पितामह ..
4.93.m: "I cry for a name; give me a name, grandfather of my creator!"
Because of his crying, the infant obtained the name Rudra.
Agastya said:
"Why did the Lord cry, O six-faced one, even after becoming a child?

4.93.s: yadi vetsi tadācakṣva mahatkautūhalaṃ hi me .. 11 ..
4.93.d: यदि वेत्सि तदाचक्ष्व महत्कौतूहलं हि मे .. 11 ..
4.93.m: If you know, then tell me, for great is my curiosity."
Skanda said:
"Being the son of the omniscient one, I understand a little.
I shall tell the cause of the crying; listen, O jar-born one!
Such a thought arose in the mind of the god, the supreme self:
'Ah, to behold the magnificence of intellect of this Parameṣṭhin,
of Brahmā, the four-faced ruler of Satyaloka!'
From such joy a flood of tears welled up in the Great Lord.
Agastya said:

4.93.s:
kiṃ buddhivaibhavaṃ dhātuḥ śaṃbhunā manasīkṣitam .
yenānaṃdāśru saṃbhāro bālyepyabhavadīśituḥ ..15..
4.93.d:
किं बुद्धिवैभवं धातुः शंभुना मनसीक्षितम् .
येनानंदाश्रु संभारो बाल्येप्यभवदीशितुः ..15..
4.93.m: "What magnificence of intellect of the Creator did Śambhu behold in his mind, / on account of which an abundance of tears of joy arose in the Lord even in childhood?
Tell me this, O wise one, increaser of the joy of the omniscient!"
Having heard the words spoken by Agastya, the enemy of Tāraka said:

4.93.s: deve na manasi dhyātamiti kuṃbhajane mune ..
4.93.d: देवे न मनसि ध्यातमिति कुंभजने मुने ..
4.93.m: "This was meditated upon in his mind by the god [Brahmā], O jar-born sage: / 'Except for an offspring, who in this world is capable of redeeming his progenitor?
This is one desire; and this second one is thoroughly resolved:
when he who destroys the rebirth of him who remembers him becomes an offspring,
gazing upon him at every moment, touching his limbs at every moment,
he will obtain through him a single bed, seat, and meal at every moment!
He who is nowhere within the range even of speech and mind,
having become my offspring, what desired thing will he not bestow?

4.93.s: sa me'patyatvamāsādya kiṃ na dāsyati ciṃtitam .. 4.2.93.20 ..
4.93.d: स मेऽपत्यत्वमासाद्य किं न दास्यति चिंतितम् .. 4.2.93.20 ..
4.93.m: Whatever living being should touch him even once, or behold him even once with joy,

4.93.s:
yo'muṃ sakṛtspṛśejjaṃturyomuṃ paśyetsakṛnmudā .
na sa bhūyobhijāyeta bhaveccānaṃdameduraḥ .. 21 ..
4.93.d:
योऽमुं सकृत्स्पृशेज्जंतुर्योमुं पश्येत्सकृन्मुदा .
न स भूयोभिजायेत भवेच्चानंदमेदुरः .. 21 ..
4.93.m: he would not be born again, and he would become filled with bliss.
If somehow he should become a plaything in my house,
then I would become a receptacle of supreme happiness, without doubt.'

4.93.s: vidheḥ samīhitaṃ ceti nūnaṃ jñātvā sa sarvavit ..
4.93.d: विधेः समीहितं चेति नूनं ज्ञात्वा स सर्ववित् ..
4.93.m: Knowing indeed this intention of the Creator, that omniscient one
held three eyes filled with tears of joy.
Hearing this speech of Skanda, Agastya rejoiced greatly,
bowed at his feet, and said: 'Victory, O son of the Omniscient!

4.93.s:
vidherapi manojñātaṃ śaṃbhorapi manogatam . .
samyakcittaṃ tvayā jñātaṃ namastubhyaṃ cidātmane .. 25 ..
4.93.d:
विधेरपि मनोज्ञातं शंभोरपि मनोगतम् . .
सम्यक्चित्तं त्वया ज्ञातं नमस्तुभ्यं चिदात्मने .. 25 ..
4.93.m: The mind of Brahmā was known, and what was in Śambhu's mind was also known; / the thought was known rightly by you. Praise to you, whose essence is consciousness!'
Skanda, too, was exceedingly pleased on seeing the joy of the listener:
"Blessed are you, Agastya, blessed are you! You know how to listen truly.

4.93.s: na me śramo vṛthā jāto bruvataste puraḥ kathām ..
4.93.d: न मे श्रमो वृथा जातो ब्रुवतस्ते पुरः कथाम् ..
4.93.m: My effort has not been in vain while telling the story before you."

4.93.s:
ityagastiṃ samābhāṣya punaḥ prāha ṣaḍānanaḥ .. 27 . .
deve rudratvamāpanne devī dakṣasutābhavat ..
4.93.d:
इत्यगस्तिं समाभाष्य पुनः प्राह षडाननः .. 27 . .
देवे रुद्रत्वमापन्ने देवी दक्षसुताभवत् ..
4.93.m: Having addressed Agastya thus, the six-faced one spoke again: / "When the god had attained rudra-hood, the goddess became the daughter of Dakṣa.

4.93.s: sāpi taptvā tapastīvraṃ satī kāśyāṃ varārthinī .. 28 ..
4.93.d: सापि तप्त्वा तपस्तीव्रं सती काश्यां वरार्थिनी .. 28 ..
4.93.m: She too, desiring a boon, performed severe austerity in Kāśī, as Satī.
She saw Hara manifested before her in the form of a liṅga,
who clearly said: 'Enough of performing austerity, O Great Goddess!

4.93.s: idaṃ satīśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ tava nāmnā bhaviṣyati ...
4.93.d: इदं सतीश्वरं लिंगं तव नाम्ना भविष्यति ...
4.93.m: This liṅga shall be named Satīśvara after your name.
Just as your desire has borne fruit here, O daughter of Dakṣa,
so too, by worshipping this liṅga, it shall bear fruit for another as well.
A maiden shall obtain a husband exalted beyond even the mind's wish.
By worshipping this liṅga, a youth also [shall obtain] an excellent woman.

4.93.s: yasya yasya hi yaḥ kāmastasya tasya hi sa dhruvam .. 32 ..
4.93.d: यस्य यस्य हि यः कामस्तस्य तस्य हि स ध्रुवम् .. 32 ..
4.93.m: Whatever desire whoever has, that indeed surely
shall be fulfilled through the worship of Satīśvara, without doubt.

4.93.s: satīśvaraṃ samabhyarcya yo yo yaṃ yaṃ samīhate .. 33 ..
4.93.d: सतीश्वरं समभ्यर्च्य यो यो यं यं समीहते .. 33 ..
4.93.m: Having worshipped Satīśvara, whatever whichever person desires,

4.93.s: tasya tasya sa sa kṣipraṃ bhaviṣyati manorathaḥ .. 34 ..
4.93.d: तस्य तस्य स स क्षिप्रं भविष्यति मनोरथः .. 34 ..
4.93.m: that desire of his shall be quickly fulfilled.
And on the eighth day from now, Prajāpati, your father,

4.93.s: mahyaṃ dāsyati kanyāṃ tvāṃ saphalaste manorathaḥ ..
4.93.d: मह्यं दास्यति कन्यां त्वां सफलस्ते मनोरथः ..
4.93.m: will give you, as a maiden, to me; your desire is fruitful.'"

4.93.s:
ityuktvā devadeveśastatraivāṃtarhitobhavat .. 35 . .
sāpi svabhavanaṃ yātā satī dākṣāyaṇī mudā . .
pitāpi tasmai prādāttāṃ rudrāya divaseṣṭame .. 36 ..
4.93.d:
इत्युक्त्वा देवदेवेशस्तत्रैवांतर्हितोभवत् .. 35 . .
सापि स्वभवनं याता सती दाक्षायणी मुदा . .
पितापि तस्मै प्रादात्तां रुद्राय दिवसेष्टमे .. 36 ..
4.93.m: Having spoken thus, the Lord of the god of gods vanished right there. / She too, Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, went to her own abode with joy. / Her father also gave her to that Rudra on the eighth day.
Skanda said:
"Thus the Satīśvara liṅga appeared in Kāśī, O sage.
Even from remembrance, the liṅga will grant the supreme quality of sattva.

4.93.s:
ratneśātpūrvato bhāge dṛṣṭvā liṃgaṃ satīśvaram . .
mucyate pātakaiḥ sadyaḥ kramājjñānaṃ ca viṃdati .. 38 .. ..
4.93.d:
रत्नेशात्पूर्वतो भागे दृष्ट्वा लिंगं सतीश्वरम् . .
मुच्यते पातकैः सद्यः क्रमाज्ज्ञानं च विंदति .. 38 .. ..
4.93.m: Seeing the Satīśvara liṅga to the east of Ratneśa, / one is immediately freed from sins and gradually attains knowledge."

Long ago, there was a sage here named Sanāru, living as a householder.
Constantly devoted to the recitation of the Vedas, and constantly honoring guests as deities,
constantly engaged in worshipping the liṅga, and constantly refusing gifts at sacred fords.
To that seer Sanāru was born a son named Upajaṅghani.
Once he went to the forest, and there he was bitten by a serpent.

Heaving sighs, Sanāru carried that Upajaṅghani

4.94.m: Then, seeing that Upajaṅghani

and brought it right there, and it too, reviving, departed from that place.
Then the sage, realizing the truth indicated by the reviving,
as the sage gently dug with the palm of his hand,

4.94.m: Formerly, while Viṣṇu was performing tapas here, that liṅga indeed

on the bank of the Cakrapuṣkariṇī, his attainment is not far off.
And among these fourteen liṅgas, O best of men,
the group of eight liṅgas is of great potency, a forest-fire to the seeds of past actions.
The fourteen liṅgas that have been mentioned, beginning with Oṃkāra,
and the eight great liṅgas beginning with Dakṣeśvara,
and likewise the fourteen liṅgas beginning with Śailaiśa—
these thirty-six together bring about the complete attainment of the sacred field.

dwelling eternally in this sacred field, imparts liberating knowledge.

From worshipping them, misfortune will never come to men.
O sage, these liṅgas are secret mysteries, assuredly;
and by the power of these liṅgas, liberation here is entirely certain.
This Kāśī is the sacred field of liberation on account of these liṅgas, O highly intelligent one.
These and other perfected ones arise age after age.
This Ānandakānana, Śambhu's sacred field, is beginningless;

4.94.m: those who attain a dwelling here are liberated indeed, without a doubt.
Here indeed is the perfection of yoga; here alone is the perfection of tapas;
the perfection of vows, the perfection of mantras, and the perfection of the sacred ford are fully assured.
The group of eight perfections that is spoken of, the great [powers] beginning with animā—
this very garden of bliss of Śambhu is their birthplace.
This Ānandakānana is the dwelling of the goddess of ultimate release.
Having attained it through merits, one who fears worldly existence must not abandon it.
This alone is the greatest gain; this alone is the supreme tapas;
this alone is the great merit: that Vārāṇasī has been reached here.
Death will inevitably come to an embodied being somewhere or other;

one must necessarily resort to Kāśikā, which removes all karmic consequences.

4.95.m: Listen, Sūta of great intelligence, as it was spoken by Skanda
concerning my future before that great-minded jar-born [Agastya].
Skanda said:
Hear, O fortunate sage, son of Mitra and Varuṇa,
how the best of sages, the son of Parāśara, will fall into delusion.
The highly intelligent one, having divided the Vedas according to the differences of various recensions,
and having taught the eighteen Purāṇas to Sūta and others,
who composed the secret of the Vedas, smṛtis, and Purāṇas,
and [the work] named Mahābhārata, delighting all worlds,
which calms all sins, produces supreme peace for all,
and by the mere hearing of which the killing of a brahmin is destroyed.
Once that glorious sage, wandering over the surface of the earth,
reached Naimiṣāraṇya, where lords of sages dwell:
eighty-eight thousand [sages] whose wealth was austerity, led by Śaunaka, / with broad foreheads marked by the three horizontal stripes, wearing radiant garlands of rudrākṣa beads,
bearing sacred ash, devotedly fond of reciting the Rudrasūkta,
intent on worshipping the liṅga, reverent toward the name of Śiva,

4.95.s: eka eva hi viśveśo muktido nānya eva hi ..
4.95.d: एक एव हि विश्वेशो मुक्तिदो नान्य एव हि ..
4.95.m: saying constantly: "Only the Lord of All gives liberation, indeed no one else!"
—with their minds fully resolved.
Seeing all of them devoted in soul to Giriśa, the sage Vyāsa,
raising his forefinger high, spoke this speech in turn:
"Having thoroughly churned the net of speech, having determined repeatedly and deeply,
this one thing is ascertained: Hari, the Lord of all, is to be served.

4.95.m: In the Veda, in the Rāmāyaṇa, in the Purāṇas, and in the [Mahā]bhārata,
at the beginning, middle, and end, Hari alone is [proclaimed] here, no other.

4.95.s: satyaṃ satyaṃ trisatyaṃ punaḥ satyaṃ na mṛṣā punaḥ ..
4.95.d: सत्यं सत्यं त्रिसत्यं पुनः सत्यं न मृषा पुनः ..
4.95.m: It is true, true, thrice true, true again, never false:

4.95.s: na vedādaparaṃ śāstraṃ na devocyutataḥ paraḥ .. 13 ..
4.95.d: न वेदादपरं शास्त्रं न देवोच्युततः परः .. 13 ..
4.95.m: there is no scripture higher than the Veda; there is no deity higher than Acyuta.
The Lord of Lakṣmī bestows all, no other; the Lord of Lakṣmī also grants final emancipation.

4.95.m: Only the Lord of Lakṣmī is one; therefore he alone should be meditated upon, and no other.

Those dull-witted who, having abandoned [him], worship someone other than Keśava,
enter again and again into the impenetrable cycle of transmigration.

4.95.s: eka eva hi sarveśo hṛṣīkeśaḥ parātparaḥ ..

4.95.m: Only Hṛṣīkeśa is the Lord of all, higher than the highest;
one who serves him constantly becomes worthy of worship by the three worlds.

4.95.m: Go to Vārāṇasī, O Vyāsa, where Viśveśvara himself is present;

4.95.m: Reaching Vārāṇasī, Vyāsa bathed in the pool of the Pañcanada,
worshipped the glorious Mādhava, and then went to Pādodaka.

Delighted by the sounding of conches before and behind, [he cried]:
"Victory, O Viṣṇu, Hṛṣīkeśa, Govinda, Madhusūdana,
Acyuta, Ananta, Vaikuṇṭha, Mādhava, Upendra, Keśava,
Trivikrama, mace-handed one, bow-handed one, Janārdana,

Nārāyaṇa, enemy of the Asuras, Kṛṣṇa, Śauri, four-armed one,
delight of Devakī's heart, increaser of Yaśodā's joy,
